what_it_does: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) is a fundamental mathematical operation that breaks a matrix — a grid of numbers — into three simpler pieces; it is widely used in signal processing, recommendation engines, and compressing AI models. The problem is that SVD scales very badly: doubling the size of the input matrix makes the computation roughly eight times larger (it grows with the cube of the input size), so real-time applications need dedicated hardware. This paper builds a specialized accelerator on a Xilinx Versal chip, which is a hybrid device that combines a traditional programmable logic fabric with built-in, hard-wired AI compute engines (called AIE, or AI Engines) on the same chip. The design co-optimizes the SVD algorithm itself (in particular the ordering of its iterative refinement steps) alongside the hardware layout, funneling the right work to the right unit. An automatic tuning framework explores the design space to find the best combination of performance, latency, and power, targeting applications that need SVD results quickly.
